notes: Dev-split ABox revision (14 queries, all determinate, no worlds); the edit carries functional: has_spin gives one spin per kind of particle, so the stored "the photon has spin 1" is overturned (related near). Related far asks the stored "the photon is a boson", which the spin-statistics rule (half-integer spin means fermion) overturns; a model that keeps it holds a boson with half-integer spin, which no world allows, so it is determinate. A second stored route back, recorded as a residual risk: the photon is a gauge boson and gauge bosons have spin 1; after the edit that class rule must give way for the photon (or the photon leaves the gauge bosons), and either way the photon has half-integer spin, so "fermion" still follows. The new world contradicts other firm facts about light (lasers and Bose-Einstein statistics of photons rely on photons being bosons); those are consequences of the same class rule, so they move with the edit rather than giving a second answer, and no query asks them. Derived: the Pauli principle by inheritance; whether the Dirac equation describes the photon (inheritance through another class rule of spin-1/2 particles, not the spin-statistics one; it replaced a 720-degree rotation question after the audit, since the models did not hold the 720-degree rule); and binding through the description "the quantum of light", which the model holds separately and which carries no class rule that fixes spin. Changed in review: a comparison with the electron's spin (labelled composition, but a join of two values, not a second fact about the new value) and a binding through "the particle that carries the electromagnetic force" (force carriers are gauge bosons, which have spin 1, a stored route back to the old answer) were replaced. Near unrelated: the Higgs boson's spin (0) shares the relation, is untouched, and differs from the new answer; the electron was not used there because its spin equals the new answer. Counts are exact-phrase Dolma counts unless marked approximate.
